target: Paso por tu casa a las ocho.
english: I'll swing by your house at eight.
tip: "Por" = through/along: "Caminamos por el parque." Por for movement through or past a place.

target: No le digas nada, es una sorpresa.
english: Don't tell him anything, it's a surprise.
tip: Double negatives are correct Spanish! 'No le digas nada' = don't tell him NOTHING. After no, everything else goes negative too – nada, nunca, nadie.

target: Probé la comida local y me encantó.
english: I tried the local food and loved it.
tip: 'Me encantó' flips the sentence: the FOOD did the enchanting, to me. Like gustar, encantar makes the thing you love the subject – you're just the target.

target: Ayer hubo un problema con el sistema.
english: Yesterday there was a problem with the system.
tip: Hubo = pretérito of haber (there was/were). Singular form even for plurals.

target: La casa donde crecí ya no existe.
english: The house where I grew up no longer exists.
tip: 'Ya' means already – but 'ya no' flips to 'not anymore.' 'Ya no existe' = it no longer exists, not 'it already doesn't exist.'

target: Le dieron gato por liebre en esa tienda.
english: They ripped him off at that store.
tip: Literally 'they gave him cat for hare' – medieval inns passed off cat as hare meat. 'Dar gato por liebre' = rip someone off with a fake.

target: Encontré un billete de cincuenta en la calle.
english: I found a fifty-euro note on the street.
tip: 'Billete' is both ticket AND banknote. 'Un billete de cincuenta' = a fifty-euro bill – context (and the number) tells you which one you found.

target: Aunque no tenía experiencia, le dieron el puesto.
english: Even though he had no experience, they gave him the position.
tip: "Aunque" + indicative = although (known fact): "Aunque llueve, salgo." Compare: aunque + subjunctive = even if (hypothetical).

target: Mientras leía el periódico, alguien tocó la puerta.
english: While I was reading the newspaper, someone knocked on the door.
tip: 'Tocó la puerta' – nobody touched the door. Tocar covers touch, play music, and KNOCK. At a door, tocar means someone's knocking.

target: Habrán sido las tres cuando llegamos al pueblo.
english: It must have been about three when we arrived at the town.
tip: 'Habrán sido las tres' – future tense about the past?! Spanish uses future for guessing: 'it will have been three' = it must have been around three.

target: El agua está fría hoy, pero ayer estaba caliente.
english: The water is cold today, but yesterday it was hot.
tip: "El agua"... but "fría"? Agua is feminine – it borrows el only because the stressed a- start would clash with la. Adjectives stay feminine: el agua está fría.

target: Mientras esperaba el autobús, vi a un viejo amigo.
english: While I was waiting for the bus, I saw an old friend.
tip: Imperfect (esperaba) for ongoing wait + preterite (vi) for the sudden encounter.

target: Nos hicimos una foto con la torre de fondo.
english: We took a photo with the tower in the background.
tip: Spaniards don't 'take' photos – they MAKE them, on themselves: 'nos hicimos una foto' = we made ourselves a photo. Tomar una foto reads Latin American.

target: Mientras mi madre cocinaba, mi padre puso la mesa.
english: While my mother was cooking, my father set the table.
tip: Imperfect (cocinaba) for ongoing background + preterite (puso) for completed action.

target: Me dejó plantado; esperé una hora y no vino.
english: He stood me up (lit. he left me planted) – i waited an hour and he didn't come.
tip: 'Plantado' = planted. 'Me dejó plantado' = he stood me up – literally 'he left me planted', stuck waiting where you stood.

target: La razón por la cual cerró la tienda fue económica.
english: The reason the store closed was financial.
tip: "Por la cual" = for which (formal): "La razón por la cual..." More literary than "por la que" but same meaning.

target: Solía acostarme muy tarde, pero ahora intento dormirme antes de las once.
english: I used to go to bed very late, but now I try to fall asleep before eleven.
tip: "Solía" is the imperfect of "soler" – used for past habits that no longer continue. "I used to go to bed late (but not anymore)."

target: Hicimos un álbum de fotos familiar para el aniversario de bodas de mis padres.
english: We made a family photo album for my parents' wedding anniversary.
tip: One wedding, plural noun: it's aniversario de bodas. Bodas comes from Latin vota – the wedding vows, plural – so wedding phrases keep the -s.

target: Lo firmó el director esta mañana.
english: The director signed it this morning.
tip: 'Lo firmó el director' – the doer comes LAST. 'Lo' already told you what got signed, so Spanish happily parks el director after the verb.

target: Le puso verde delante de todos en la oficina.
english: She badmouthed him in front of everyone at the office.
tip: 'Le puso verde' = literally 'she turned him green'. Poner verde a alguien = trash-talk them mercilessly – a color idiom English lacks; this green has nothing to do with envy.

target: Viajamos por carretera.
english: We traveled by road.
tip: "Por" = via / by way of: "Fuimos por la autopista." Por for the route or means of travel.

target: Te llamo por teléfono.
english: I'll call you by phone.
tip: "Por" = via: "Lo dije por teléfono." Por for the method of communication.

target: Se nos acabó la leche.
english: We ran out of milk.
tip: "Se nos acabó" – "se" construction for unplanned events.

target: Le pasé tu número al cliente.
english: I gave your number to the client.
tip: Saying 'to him' twice? Normal. 'Le pasé tu número al cliente' – Spanish keeps the pronoun 'le' even when 'al cliente' spells out exactly who.

target: No pude dormir en toda la noche.
english: I couldn't sleep all night.
tip: In the preterite, poder means managed to. 'No pude dormir' = I tried and failed to sleep that night – a one-off defeat, not general inability.

target: Mis padres se conocieron en una fiesta.
english: My parents met each other at a party.
tip: Conocerse (reciprocal preterite): se conocieron – they met each other.

target: Me equivoqué de dirección y me perdí.
english: I got the address wrong and got lost.
tip: Wrong address? Spanish says you mistook yourself OF it: 'me equivoqué de dirección.' Equivocarse de + noun = get the wrong X, any X.

target: Por favor, envíeme el informe antes del mediodía.
english: Please send me the report before noon.
tip: 'Envíeme,' not 'envíame' – that -e ending is the usted command. One vowel signals professional distance; use it with clients and strangers.

target: Por eso no pude ir a la cena.
english: That's why I couldn't go to the dinner.
tip: "Por eso" = that's why / because of that. Connects a cause to its consequence: "Llovía, por eso me quedé."

target: Me quedé boquiabierto.
english: I was speechless.
tip: "Boquiabierto" – literally "open-mouthed"; stunned.
